judged_text: The booking record still connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, so the multi-host destination calendar list this PR introduces has no durable representation anywhere in the data model. Every post-creation flow (reschedule, cancel, reminders, payment webhooks) rebuilds destinationCalendar as a single-element array from booking.destinationCalendar, so the collective multi-host state exists only in memory during the initial create and cannot be audited or recovered from the booking afterwards.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` changed to an array and `handleNewBooking` can push additional team members’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), but when persisting the booking it still connects only the first element (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`). Many later flows rebuild `destinationCalendar` as a single-element array from `booking.destinationCalendar`/`user.destinationCalendar` (e.g., cron reminder, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, confirm/editLocation/cancel). This is a real, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern: the expanded list is not persisted in the booking’s `destinationCalendar` relation, so consumers relying on that field won’t see the multi-host state post-create. However, the claim that there’s “no durable representation anywhere” is somewhat overstated because calendar targets may still be inferable from stored booking calendar references (`booking.references.filter(..."_calendar")`).
